draft.title: Minerals
card: Minerals are nutrients the body needs in small amounts. They do not give energy, but the body needs them to work.
helps build and keep strong bones and teeth. Dairy foods are a common source.
helps blood carry oxygen around the body. Red meat, beans and spinach contain it.
helps keep the balance of fluid in the body. Salt is the main source in most diets.
draft.remember: Each mineral has its own job: calcium for bones, iron for oxygen, sodium for fluid balance.

a.q: Which mineral helps the blood carry oxygen around the body?
a.why: Iron helps blood carry oxygen. Calcium is tempting because it is a well-known mineral, but its job is to build and keep bones and teeth strong.
a.clue: Red meat and spinach contain it.

b.q: Tom wants to keep his bones strong as he grows. Which choice best fits the mineral job he needs?
opts: Eat more dairy foods for calcium
Eat more red meat for sodium
Eat more spinach for fluid balance
b.why: Calcium builds and keeps strong bones and teeth, and dairy foods are a common source. Salt gives sodium, which is linked to fluid balance, not bones.
b.clue: Match the mineral to bones, then pick its source.

b.best: Eat more dairy foods for calcium
